newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 25.

text.p: Affiliates of Exxon Corp -- Esso Sekiyu KK, General Sekiyu KK and Tonen Corp -- plan to jointly set up a special group on October 1 to start business negotiating construction orders and material procurement. The plan is to cut prices following deregulation of gasoline imports to Japan in April. Esso and General Sekiyu have already set up a group operating at Esso Sekiyu headquarters. Tonen plans to join the company in October.

Six communication equipment makers, inculding Anritsu Corp, are expected to see improved current earnings in the business year to next March 31, helped by expansion of mobile phone-related equipment and growing digital-communication markets. Anritsu is expected to increase its current profit by 25 percent from a year earlier. Anritsu expects the mobile phone market to expand by nearly 20 percent and sees its sales sales rising 11 percent from a year earlier.

Tokyo Senpaku Kaisha Ltd, a shipping group company of Nippon Yusen KK, has built up a container route network covering almost the whole of Southeast Asia, in cooperation with Thai and Indonesian shipping companies. It plans to provide a better service for Japanese manufacturers relocating their production bases in the region.

Nissho Iwai Corp has invested about 200 million yen in a chemical company in New Zealand to produce lithium carbonate powder, used in lithium batteries. It targets annual output of 3,000 tonnes of lithium powder from next April.
NEC Corp to sell 20.1-inch colour liquid crystal displays (LCDs) designed for desktop-type personal computers from January 1997. It hopes to sell 5,000 units a month at a cost of under 500,000 yen.

Mitsubishi Corp will enter the hospital meals business on Wednesday in a joint venture with its group company and French catering firm Sodexho. The new firm, capitalised at 200 million yen, will be owned 40 percent each by Mitsubishi and Sodexho and 20 percent by the group company.

Isetan Co Ltd is to take legal action against Barney's Inc, a U.S. luxury clothing retailer, in response to Barney's demands to terminate its licensing agreement with Isetan. Isetan is ready to sue Barney's as early as this month.
